title: Training and Strategies for Handling Prison Inmates with Intellectual Disability
what_it_is: Training and Strategies for Handling Prison Inmates with Intellectual Disability

sections.label: Prison Officer Course training
sections.summary: New officers undergo Prison Officer Course training to develop understanding of their needs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: New officers undergo training as part of the Prison Officer Course to develop understanding of their needs.

sections.label: Support for inmates with disabilities
sections.summary: SPS works with MINDS on officer training and modifies rehabilitation services and programmes for inmates with intellectual disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Since 2022, the Singapore Prison Service (SPS) has also worked with the Movement for the Intellectually Disabled of Singapore to provide training for officers in areas like communication and behavioural management.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For inmates with intellectual disabilities, SPS modifies the content and delivery of rehabilitation services and programmes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For example, correctional rehabilitation specialists and psychologists who conduct the psychological-based correctional programmes would deliver the content to such inmates using bite-sized information, supplementary visual aids and simplified language, or they would slow down the sessions to make it easier for the inmates to understand the content.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For those who are assessed to have adjustment issues, such as difficulties with being separated from their caregivers, SPS officers will engage them more frequently in order to better understand their needs and support them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For inmates with more complex needs, SPS adopts a multidisciplinary team (MDT) approach.

sections.label: Inmate abuse reporting channels
sections.summary: Inmates can report abuse to prison officers or Correctional Unit Officers, and cells have distress intercoms for immediate assistance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Inmates can report abuse through various channels, such as to the prison officers on duty at their Correctional Unit or during their regular engagements with their respective Correctional Unit Officers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In addition, inmates' cells are equipped with distress intercoms which inmates can activate if they require immediate assistance.
